title: Qu'est-ce qu'une famille?
oneGoal: Students will understand that families come in many different forms and all families are special and important
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students sharing about their family structure?
What level of emotional support do students need when discussing family?
Should we focus on similarities or differences in families first?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes that all families are valuable regardless of their structure
realWorldConnection: Every person belongs to a family that loves and cares for them in their own special way

title: Ma famille à moi
oneGoal: Students will share and celebrate their own family structure and members with pride and confidence
decisionPoints: How do we ensure all family structures feel valued and included?
Should students draw, tell, or show photos of their families?
How do we handle sensitive family situations with care?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by moving from general family concepts to personal family identity and pride
realWorldConnection: Being proud of our family helps us feel confident and secure in who we are

title: Les personnes dans ma famille
oneGoal: Students will identify different family members and understand the special relationships within families
decisionPoints: Which family roles are most common in our classroom community?
How do we include non-traditional family structures in our vocabulary?
Should we focus on roles or names first?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by exploring specific family relationships and the special bonds between family members
realWorldConnection: Each family member has a special place and important role in the family

title: Qui fait quoi dans ma famille?
oneGoal: Students will explore different family roles and understand how everyone contributes to family life
decisionPoints: How do we present family work without reinforcing gender stereotypes?
Should we focus on traditional chores or emotional support roles?
How do we include children's contributions to family work?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by examining what family members do together and how everyone has important jobs
realWorldConnection: Families work best when everyone helps and contributes in their own special way

title: Comment ma famille prend soin de moi
oneGoal: Students will recognize the many ways their family members care for and support them
decisionPoints: How do we highlight care without making students feel guilty about family challenges?
Should we focus on physical care or emotional care first?
How do we ensure students from all family situations feel included?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by focusing specifically on how family members show love and provide care
realWorldConnection: Being cared for by family helps us grow strong, healthy, and confident

title: Comment j'aide ma famille
oneGoal: Students will identify ways they contribute to their family and understand their important role as family members
decisionPoints: What level of responsibility do Grade 1 students actually have at home?
Should we focus on helping tasks or emotional contributions?
How do we make students feel valuable without overwhelming them?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by shifting focus to students' own contributions and value within their families
realWorldConnection: Even young people have important ways to help and support their families

title: Les familles de mes amis
oneGoal: Students will explore and appreciate the diversity of family structures in their classroom community
decisionPoints: How do we celebrate differences without making any student feel 'different'?
Should students share about friends' families or discuss in general terms?
How do we handle sensitive information about other families?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by expanding perspective beyond own family to appreciate family diversity in community
realWorldConnection: Learning about different families helps us understand and appreciate our community better

title: Les traditions de ma famille
oneGoal: Students will identify and share family traditions and understand how traditions connect families across time
decisionPoints: How do we include families with few established traditions or recent immigration?
Should we focus on holiday traditions or daily family habits?
How do we help students see that all family practices can be traditions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by exploring the special practices that make each family unique and connected
realWorldConnection: Family traditions help us remember who we are and stay connected to our family history

title: Comment ma famille célèbre
oneGoal: Students will explore different ways families celebrate special moments and understand celebration as family bonding
decisionPoints: How do we include families who celebrate in quiet or non-religious ways?
Should we focus on big celebrations or small daily moments?
How do we ensure religious and cultural sensitivity?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by examining how families mark special times and create joyful memories together
realWorldConnection: Celebrating together helps families feel close and creates happy memories to treasure

title: La nourriture dans ma famille
oneGoal: Students will explore family food traditions and understand how sharing meals connects families
decisionPoints: How do we handle students with food insecurity or dietary restrictions sensitively?
Should we focus on special occasion foods or daily family meals?
How do we celebrate cultural food diversity without exoticizing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by exploring how families share food and create connection through eating together
realWorldConnection: Sharing food is one of the ways families show love and stay connected every day

title: Où vit ma famille?
oneGoal: Students will explore different types of homes and understand that all homes provide families with shelter and belonging
decisionPoints: How do we discuss housing without highlighting economic differences?
Should we focus on house types or what makes a place feel like home?
How do we include students whose housing situation may be unstable?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by exploring the physical spaces where families live and feel secure together
realWorldConnection: Having a safe place to live with family helps us feel secure and ready to learn and grow

title: Les espaces spéciaux de ma famille
oneGoal: Students will identify special family spaces and understand how physical spaces can hold family memories and meaning
decisionPoints: How do we help students find meaning in any family space, regardless of size or luxury?
Should we focus on rooms, outdoor spaces, or specific objects?
How do we include students who may not have permanent family spaces?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by examining how specific places within homes become meaningful to families
realWorldConnection: Special family spaces help us feel connected to our family and hold our important memories

title: Comment les familles communiquent
oneGoal: Students will explore different ways families communicate and understand communication as essential for family connection
decisionPoints: How do we include families who communicate in multiple languages?
Should we focus on verbal communication or include non-verbal family communication?
How do we address students whose families may have communication challenges?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by exploring how families stay connected through talking, listening, and understanding
realWorldConnection: Good communication helps families solve problems, share love, and stay close to each other

title: Les familles dans notre communauté
oneGoal: Students will understand how families connect with other families and contribute to community life
decisionPoints: How connected are students' families to the local community?
Should we focus on neighborhood connections or broader community involvement?
How do we include families who may be isolated or new to the community?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by expanding family connections beyond the home to community relationships
realWorldConnection: Families are stronger when they connect with other families and help their community

title: Créer un livre de famille
oneGoal: Students will create a family book celebrating their family's unique story and characteristics
decisionPoints: What format would work best for students with different fine motor skills?
Should books focus on current family or include family history?
How do we support students who may need help gathering family information?
progression: Extension activity that synthesizes Lessons 1-14 by creating a personal family celebration project
realWorldConnection: Creating family stories helps us remember and share what makes our family special

title: Exposition de familles
oneGoal: Students will share their family celebrations with classmates and appreciate the diversity of all families
decisionPoints: How do we create a safe, celebratory atmosphere for family sharing?
Should presentations be formal or informal, individual or small group?
How do we ensure all families feel equally celebrated and valued?
progression: Extension activity building on Lesson 15 by sharing family stories and appreciating classroom family diversity
realWorldConnection: Sharing our family stories helps others understand and appreciate different ways of being a family

title: Jeu de rôles: Ma famille
oneGoal: Students will role-play family scenarios to practice family vocabulary and explore family relationships
decisionPoints: Which family scenarios would be most engaging and appropriate for role-play?
Should students play their own family roles or explore different family structures?
How do we keep role-play respectful and inclusive of all family types?
progression: Extension activity building on all previous lessons by practicing family concepts through creative play
realWorldConnection: Playing family roles helps us understand different perspectives and practice family relationships

title: Lettres à ma famille
oneGoal: Students will write simple letters to family members expressing appreciation and love
decisionPoints: What writing level is appropriate for Grade 1 students' letter writing?
Should letters focus on gratitude, love, or sharing school learning?
How do we support students who may need help expressing their feelings?
progression: Extension activity building on communication themes from Lesson 13 by practicing family appreciation
realWorldConnection: Telling family members how we feel about them helps strengthen family relationships

title: Célébration des familles
oneGoal: Students will plan and participate in a classroom celebration honoring all types of families
decisionPoints: What type of celebration would include and honor all family structures?
Should families be invited to participate or should this be a classroom-only event?
How do we ensure the celebration feels joyful and inclusive for everyone?
progression: Extension activity culminating unit learning by celebrating family diversity in a community event
realWorldConnection: Celebrating families together helps us appreciate that all families are important and valuable

title: Je suis fier de ma famille
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their learning about families and express pride in their own family relationships
decisionPoints: How do we help students articulate what they've learned about families?
Should reflection focus on personal growth or family appreciation?
How do we end the unit with confidence and family pride for all students?
progression: Extension activity concluding the unit by celebrating personal family pride and learning growth
realWorldConnection: Being proud of our family gives us confidence and helps us appreciate other families too
